253Propose h10FINAL: Real dissipated power is ~1.10x the model's power gains on all blocks (global power-delivery gain fault, beyond the 4% spec tolerance). Model power gains are ~9% too low: model/reality = 1/1.10 - 1 ≈ −0.091. Verified by fits at nominal/cores-max/peripherals-max/min power; time constants unchanged (m3/m5/m14), so it is a power gain error, not a conductance error.
254Propose h11FINAL: l3-region model fault — the model's l3 boundary conductance (b_l3, R=1.745 originally) is too high; reality is more resistive (R≈4.2), i.e. conductance ≈1.745/4.2 − 1 ≈ −0.58 (model too high by ~58%). Raising b_l3 to 4.2 fixed the l3-adjacent core elevation (c1,c3,c5,c6) and T_package excess simultaneously, with all sensors then within ~1°C of observation. T_core1's apparent anomaly and T_package's apparent excess were both explained by this single model fault — no instrument faults beyond spec remain.
255Propose h12FINAL: core7-region lateral spreading fault — the model's silicon-level lateral edges from si_core7 (lsi_core7__l3, lsi_core6__core7, lsi_misc__core7, lsi_uncore__core7) are too resistive; conductances roughly 3-5x stronger in reality (R: 22.01→4.0, 12.57→2.5, 7.15→1.5, 6.48→1.3). Fits all four c7 observations (own-power, nominal, peripherals-max, cores-max) within ~1°C. Core7's real power, vertical path and boundary are normal (r52-r65 ruled out alternatives).
256Answer 1model · global · global power-delivery gain fault: every block dissipates ~10% more real power than the model's power_gain entry represents · -0.09
model · l3 block boundary edge b_l3 · l3 boundary conductance too high in model: real TIM escape path at ihs_l3 is more resistive (R 1.745 -> ~4.2), elevating l3-adjacent cores and the package · -0.58
model · core7 silicon lateral edges (lsi_core7__l3, lsi_core6__core7, lsi_misc__core7, lsi_uncore__core7) · lateral silicon spreading conductance from si_core7 too low in model: reality roughly 3-5x more conductive, so core7 hotspot spreads wider and runs ~3-4C cooler · -0.7		✗ wrongh10, h11, h12

The c1 elevation at nominal/cores-max/peripherals-max (+2 to +3) needs a mechanism that scales with total power in the l3/mc region — consistent with b_l3 degradation. The c7 misfit is NOT visible here either (c7 fits within 0.3 when core7 is at min power and only lateral inflow matters). The c7 misfit appears ONLY when core7 is the heat source (own-power m21: −3.8, nominal −1.5) — supporting a core7-specific spreading fault, NOT a sensor fault (a sensor fault would show at all workloads).

Model/reality conductance error = 1.60563/0.5 − 1 ≈ +2.21 (model too resistive / too low conductance, positive in conductance sense).

431NoteK-MATRIX SESSION. Residuals (obs avg − factory t_amb=0 prediction), 5 workloads in [cores-max, core7-only, nominal, all-min, periph-max], per sensor: c0: [6.79, 2.53, 4.80, 2.15, 4.32] c1: [5.88, 2.89, 5.58, 2.05, 5.06] c2: [6.17, 2.55, 5.79, 2.06, 4.89] c3: [5.80, 2.72, 5.11, 1.87, 5.02] c4: [6.30, 2.51, 4.97, 2.38, 5.24] c5: [5.77, 3.02, 5.18, 1.88, 5.18] c6: [5.24, 3.09, 4.68, 1.77, 5.31] c7: [2.91, 2.62, 4.58, 1.97, 5.19] pkg:[6.23, 2.90, 6.06, 1.84, 4.95] All-min residual ≈ sensor offsets+ambient: c7 highest 1.97, c3/c5/c6 lowest ~1.8, others ~2.1, pkg 1.84, spread 0.4°C (within calib-resid ≤0.3 + amb drift + quantization avg ±0.29; marginal but OK). Core pattern: c7 runs ~3.3° cooler than the pack at cores-max (its 2.91 vs others ~6), and ~2.4 cooler at nominal — a real core7-region effect vs global ~2-5° hot reading. Everything hot vs model everywhere; periph-max and nominal show similar excess (~5), cores-max similar (~6). Query: is excess ∝ model rise (slope fault s), or a constant offset per sensor, or power-scaled? c7's deficit at high core power vs +2.6 excess at low core power is a workload-dependent sign flip — most consistent with a core7-specific conductance improvement (vertical/boundary), not a sensor slope (slope would raise c7 everywhere proportional to rise).

RESIDUALS (obs rise - model): c0 +4.3, c1 +6.1, c2 +4.8, c3 +5.7, c4 +5.7, c5 +5.4, c6 +4.3, c7 +3.6, pkg +5.3. nominal obs: 85.0, 84.33, 88.0, 83.0, 87.0, 84.0, 84.67, 78.0, 72.0; rises: 41.6, 40.9, 44.6, 39.6, 43.6, 40.6, 41.3, 34.6, 28.6. nominal model (r234): 38.59, 34.73, 40.53, 35.00, 38.68, 35.37, 36.81, 31.57, 23.89. Note earlier conflicting notebook table used ambient 42.6 -> K-session residuals ~2-3 at those workloads; with ambient 43.4 they become +3-6. Uncertainty in ambient (~0.5) shifts all equally. KEY: residuals are positive and LARGE everywhere (up to +6), relative to model rises of 40-59 => excess ratio ~9-15%. Cannot be explained by fidelity gap 0.618. RATIO story: cores-max excess/m ~0.09-0.14, nominal ~0.09-0.18 (c1 6.2/34.7=0.18). c7 excess +3.6/+3.0 with gain already applied; at c7-only (m29-31, avg 55.67, rise ~12.6 vs model core7-only rise r210 c7 15.14 => deficit -2.5!) — c7 reads HOT vs model at high core power but COLD at its own only-power workload. Contradiction unless c7 fault is power-dependent: at c7-only neighbors are at min so lateral inflow to c7 is small and reading is below model (deficit), while at full-core loads c7 receives hot inflow and reads above. A pure c7 gain explanation can't do both. Hypothesis: c7 excess at heavy loads comes from the GLOBAL excess (~+4-5), while the c7-only deficit is a separate c7-local cooling (or gain). Model is uniformly ~10% low in power at core-heavy loads.

597NoteFINAL ANALYSIS (post m45/m46, exact-map re-derivation). Key correction: old session-3 baselines (r240) were run at the m42 map, not envelope-min — all old session-3 "differentials" were contaminated by ~1-2°C ambient drift within session 3. Only fresh m42/m43/m44/m45/m46 (same window) are trustworthy, plus c7-only s3 with neighbor-based bias correction (bias -0.7+-0.2). Exact-map residuals at v214 (uniform gain 1.109, factory edges): - s3 cores-max: non-c7 mean +0.25 -> k=1.115; s3 periph: mean -0.05 -> k=1.109; FRESH cores-max: non-c7 mean +0.44 -> k=1.120; FRESH periph: +0.22 on 6.6 -> k=1.146 (noisy). Global k ~ 1.12 +- 0.01. Model error = 1/1.12-1 = -0.107. - c7 equations (K_self=1.332 C/W from gain-differential at fixed map): (1+s)*g7 = obs_A/11.72: raw 0.797, bias-corr 0.853, m24-transient 0.80 -> central 0.81. From cores-max fresh: (1+s) = 1.043 (bias-corr A) .. 1.065 (raw). Central s=+0.05, g7_true=0.77 (factory 1.0057 -> model error +0.30, model too high). - m24 transient shape matches uniform 0.69x scaling -> amplitude (gain) fault, not structural. - T_package: fresh slopes +4.3% (cores-max, rise 30) and +4.5% (periph, rise 6.7) -> slope fault +0.04 (beyond 3% spec). - Pure v_core7-R, pure-lateral, and no-c7-fault alternatives all fail (k would need 1.17-1.19, contradicted by 8 non-c7 sensors at 1.115-1.125). - b_l3, offsets, stuck/noise sensors, ambient-only: all ruled out previously. FINAL CARD: all gains 1.12, core7 gain 0.77, factory edges. End-to-end check predictions: m43 c7 86.8 (obs 87), c0 99.3 (98), pkg 77.1 (77); m44 pkg 54.1 (54), c7 55.9 (57, 1.2sigma); c7-only 9.6 vs 10.0; nominal c7 78.6 (78). All within gap+quant+spec.
598Propose h15FINAL: global power-delivery gain fault — real dissipated power is ~1.12x the factory model's calibrated gain on every block (k = 1.109-1.146 across clean differential datasets, central 1.12). Model power gains ~10.7% too low: model/reality = 1/1.12 - 1 = -0.107 (model too low). Time constants unchanged (m3/m5/m14/m24) so it is a power gain error, not conductance.
599Propose h16FINAL: core7 power gain fault — core7's real dissipated power is ~0.77x commanded (factory model 1.0057, i.e. model ~+0.30 too high, model/reality = 1.0057/0.77 - 1). Evidence: c7-only differential deficit (obs rise 9.3-10.0 vs card 13.0, 4-6 sigma), m24 c7-only transient matches a pure amplitude scaling (0.69x, gain-type fault, not structural R/C), and fresh cores-max c7 residual -1.4 consistent. v_core7/lateral/no-fault alternatives fail the regime split (require k=1.17-1.19, contradicted by non-c7 sensors).
600Propose h17FINAL: T_core7 sensor slope fault — reads ~5% high on rise above ambient (fresh cores-max residual -1.4 on rise 40 and periph +1.5 on rise 7.5 both fit slope ~+0.05; spec max 3%). Required to reconcile the c7 regime split (cores-max wants more cooling than c7-only at fixed self-power).
601Propose h18FINAL: T_package sensor slope fault — reads ~4.4% high on rise above ambient: fresh cores-max residual +1.24 on pkg rise 30 (+4.3%) and fresh periph residual +0.30 on rise 6.7 (+4.5%), two consistent independent estimates beyond the 3% spec bound. Commit 3's +0.10 was too large.
